It is hardened and tested once, in Drydock's own suite, so every\nTarget inherits a persistence layer that has already passed rather than one re-derived from prose\non each build.\n\nThe application-facing surface is ``Database``. One attribute per declared table, one method per\ndeclared access pattern::\n\n    db = Database(dsn, SCHEMA)\n    ticket = db.tickets.get(id=7)\n    open_tickets = db.tickets.list(status=\"open\")\n\n``schema.py`` beside this file is generated from ``DATABASE.md`` and carries the tables, the\noperations, and the row types. It contains no SQL. Statements are constructed here, by the driver\nfor the engine in use, so a parameter placeholder never appears in generated code or in a caller.\n\nValues reach the database as bound parameters, never as formatted text. Identifiers cannot be\nbound in any engine, so they are taken only from the generated schema — which Drydock validated\nagainst ``^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`` before emitting it — and are quoted on the way out.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable, Mapping, Sequence\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, fields\nfrom contextlib import contextmanager, nullcontext\nimport threading\nfrom typing import Any\n\n__all__ = [\n    \"Database\",\n    \"Driver\",\n    \"Operation\",\n    \"PersistenceError\",\n    \"Schema\",\n    \"Table\",\n    \"statements\",\n    \"UnknownOperation\",\n    \"begin_acceptance_transaction\",\n    \"end_acceptance_transaction\",\n]\n\nVERBS = (\"get\", \"list\", \"create\", \"update\", \"delete\")\n#: The comparisons a declared Match term may state; anything else is refused before SQL is built.\nCOMPARISONS = (\"=\", \"<\", \"<=\", \">\", \">=\")\nDIRECTIONS = (\"asc\", \"desc\")\n\n\nclass PersistenceError(RuntimeError):\n    \"\"\"A persistence failure the caller may act on, raised in place of a driver exception.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass UnknownOperation(PersistenceError):\n    \"\"\"A verb was requested that the declaration does not grant for that table.\"\"\"\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Table:\n    \"\"\"One declared table: its columns and the column that identifies a row.\"\"\"\n\n    name: str\n    columns: tuple[str, ...]\n    primary_key: str | None = None\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Operation:\n    \"\"\"One declared access pattern, reduced to what executing it requires.\n\n    ``name`` is the method callers use and ``verb`` is its Kind, how it runs; a name that is a\n    verb runs as that verb. ``inputs`` are the parameters the caller supplies. ``match`` is the\n    equality predicate of a ``get``, ``update``, ``upsert``, or ``delete``, every field of it\n    required; a ``list`` filters on whichever inputs are supplied, and the inputs of a\n    ``create``, ``update``, or ``upsert`` outside ``match`` are the values written. ``row`` is the dataclass the operation returns, and\n    ``columns`` are its fields; an operation with no ``row`` returns a count. ``compare`` holds\n    ``(field, op, column)`` for each input compared other than by equality with its own column,\n    such as ``(\"start_date\", \">=\", \"date\")``, and ``order`` the ``(column, direction)`` sort keys\n    of a ``list``.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    identifier: str\n    table: str\n    verb: str\n    inputs: tuple[str, ...]\n    row: type | None = None\n    columns: tuple[str, ...] = ()\n    match: tuple[str, ...] = ()\n    name: str = \"\"\n    compare: tuple[tuple[str, str, str], ...] = ()\n    order: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] = ()\n\n    def keys(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:\n        \"\"\"The match fields compared by equality: what reads back the one row a write reached.\"\"\"\n        compared = {field for field, op, _ in self.compare if op != \"=\"}\n        return tuple(name for name in self.match if name not in compared)\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Schema:\n    \"\"\"The generated declaration: every table and every operation reaching one.\"\"\"\n\n    tables: tuple[Table, ...]\n    operations: tuple[Operation, ...]\n\n    def by_table(self) -> dict[str, tuple[Operation, ...]]:\n        grouped: dict[str, list[Operation]] = {table.name: [] for table in self.tables}\n        for operation in self.operations:\n            grouped.setdefault(operation.table, []).append(operation)\n        return {name: tuple(items) for name, items in grouped.items()}\n\n\nclass Driver:\n    \"\"\"Statement construction shared by every engine.\n\n    Subclasses supply connection handling and the two things engines genuinely disagree about:\n    how a parameter is spelled, and how a freshly inserted row reports its key. Everything else is\n    identical SQL, so it is written once here rather than twice in the engines.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def prepare_schema(self, sql: str) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Translate generated DDL for this engine.\"\"\"\n        return sql\n\n    #: Spelled by the DB-API driver, not by this class's callers.\n    paramstyle = \"qmark\"\n    returning = False\n\n    def connect(self) -> Any:  # pragma: no cover - engine specific\n        raise NotImplementedError\n\n    def pin(self) -> Any:  # pragma: no cover - engine specific\n        \"\"\"Serve one connection to every thread until ``close``. The acceptance harness's.\"\"\"\n        raise NotImplementedError\n\n    def identity(self) -> str:  # pragma: no cover - engine specific\n        \"\"\"Name the store, so two spellings of one DSN share one acceptance transaction.\"\"\"\n        raise NotImplementedError\n\n    def close(self) -> None:  # pragma: no cover - engine specific\n        raise NotImplementedError\n\n    def placeholder(self, index: int) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Render parameter ``index`` (0-based) in this engine's spelling.\"\"\"\n        return \"?\" if self.paramstyle == \"qmark\" else \"%s\"\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def quote(identifier: str) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Quote a declared identifier. Never called with caller-supplied text.\"\"\"\n        if not identifier.replace(\"_\", \"\").isalnum():\n            raise PersistenceError(f\"refusing unsafe identifier {identifier!r}\")\n        return f'\"{identifier}\"'\n\n    def _predicate(\n        self, names: Sequence[str], start: int = 0, compare: Sequence[tuple[str, str, str]] = ()\n    ) -> str:\n        \"\"\"``names`` are input fields; each is compared with its declared column, else its own.\"\"\"\n        by_field = {field: (op, column) for field, op, column in compare}\n        terms = []\n        for offset, name in enumerate(names):\n            op, column = by_field.get(name, (\"=\", name))\n            if op not in COMPARISONS:\n                raise PersistenceError(f\"refusing undeclared comparison VALUES ({marks})\"\n        if self.returning and key:\n            statement += f\" RETURNING {self.quote(key)}\"\n        return statement\n\n    def update(\n        self,\n        table: str,\n str:\n        \"\"\"Insert a row, or replace the Set columns of the row ``match`` identifies.\n\n        ``match`` names a declared unique key, which is what ``ON CONFLICT`` requires; SQLite\n        and PostgreSQL spell the statement identically.\n        \"\"\"\n        assigned = [name for name in columns if name not in match]\n        target = \", \".join(self.quote(name) for name in match)\n NOTHING\"\n        )\n        return f\"{self.insert(table, columns, None)} ON CONFLICT ({target}) {action}\"\n\n    def delete(\n        self, table: str, predicate: Sequence[str], compare: compare)}\"\n        return statement\n\n    def inserted_key(self, cursor: Any) -> Any:  # pragma: no cover - engine specific\n        raise NotImplementedError\n\n\nclass TableAccess:\n    \"\"\"The methods one table grants, bound from the declaration rather than defined by hand.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, table: Table, operations: Iterable[Operation], database: Database) -> None:\n        self._table = table\n        self._database = database\n        self._operations = {operation.name or operation.verb: operation for operation in operations}\n\n    def __repr__(self) -> str:\n Any]:\n        operation = self._operations.get(name)\n        if operation is None:\n            granted = \", \".join(sorted(self._operations)) or \"none\"\n            raise UnknownOperation(\n Declared: {granted}. \"\n                \"Add an access pattern to DATABASE.md rather than reaching around this class.\"\n            )\n        return lambda **arguments: self._database.run(operation, arguments)\n\n\nclass _AcceptanceTransaction:\n    \"\"\"One transaction per store, shared by every ``Database`` this process opens; never committed.\n\n    The acceptance harness begins it before a criterion runs and rolls it back when the criterion\n    ends. A crash loses nothing: an engine discards an uncommitted transaction.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self) -> None:\n        self.lock = threading.RLock()\n        self._drivers: dict[str, Driver] = {}\n\n    def join(self, driver: Driver) -> Driver:\n        with self.lock:\n            shared = self._drivers.get(driver.identity())\n            if shared is None:\n                cursor = driver.pin().cursor()\n                try:\n                    cursor.execute(\"BEGIN\")\n                finally:\n                    cursor.close()\n                shared = self._drivers[driver.identity()] = driver\n            return shared\n\n    def rollback(self) -> None:\n        failures = []\n        with self.lock:\n            for identity, driver in self._drivers.items():\n                try:\n                    cursor = driver.pin().cursor()\n                    try:\n                        cursor.execute(\"ROLLBACK\")\n                    finally:\n                        cursor.close()\n                except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - every store is still closed\n                    failures.append(f\"{identity}: {exc}\")\n                finally:\n                    driver.close()\n            self._drivers.clear()\n        if failures:\n            raise PersistenceError(\"acceptance rollback failed: \" + \"; \".join(failures))\n\n\n_harness: _AcceptanceTransaction | None = None\n\n\ndef begin_acceptance_transaction() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Join every store this process opens from now on to one transaction the harness owns.\"\"\"\n    global _harness\n    if _harness is None:\n        _harness = _AcceptanceTransaction()\n\n\ndef end_acceptance_transaction() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Roll back the harness's transaction on every store it joined.\"\"\"\n    global _harness\n    harness, _harness = _harness, None\n    if harness is not None:\n        harness.rollback()\n\n\nclass Database:\n    \"\"\"One store, presented to callers as declared tables with declared methods.\n\n    Callers construct one instance, share it freely, and call methods synchronously. Connection\n    handling is internal and may change without affecting any caller.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, dsn: str, schema: Schema, *, driver: Driver | None = None) -> None:\n        self._rollback_owner = None\n        self._schema = schema\n        driver = driver if driver is not None else open_driver(dsn)\n        self._harness = _harness\n        self._driver = self._harness.join(driver) if self._harness is not None else driver\n        grouped = schema.by_table()\n        for table in schema.tables:\n            setattr(self, table.name, TableAccess(table, grouped.get(table.name, ()), self))\n\n    @property\n    def driver(self) -> Driver:\n        if self._harness is not None:\n            raise PersistenceError(\"driver access is forbidden inside the acceptance transaction\")\n        if self._rollback_owner is not None:\n            raise PersistenceError(\"driver access is forbidden inside a rollback session\")\n        return self._driver\n\n    def close(self) -> None:\n        if self._harness is not None:\n            return  # the acceptance harness owns the shared connection\n        if self._rollback_owner is not None:\n            raise PersistenceError(\"the rollback session owns connection lifetime\")\n        self._driver.close()\n\n    @contextmanager\n    def rollback_session(self):\n        \"\"\"Use this connection for setup, behavior and assertions; always roll back.\n\n        Normal calls remain autocommitted. Do not filter, skip, or reinterpret.\n#\n# Runs ./fxrates against a fresh database initialized by the application.\n# Loads the supplied ECB files from the command line,\n# starts `./fxrates serve` on a free local port, and compares every command's exit code and\n# standard output, and every HTTP response's status and JSON body, with the known answer below.\n# JSON bodies are compared as values, so key order and whitespace do not matter. Standard error\n# and error-response bodies are never compared. No network beyond 127.0.0.1 is used.\n#\n#   sh sources/run.sh               from the application root (how `drydock uat` runs it)\n#   sh uat/FxRates/bin/run.sh APP   from anywhere, grading the application root APP\n#\n# Exit 0 only when every check passes.\nset -u\n\nHERE=$(cd \"$(dirname \"$0\")\" && pwd)\nAPP=$(cd \"${1:-.}\" && pwd)\nif [ -f \"$HERE/eurofxref-hist_2025-01.csv\" ]; then DATA=$HERE; else DATA=$(cd \"$HERE/../sources\" && pwd); fi\nWORK=$(mktemp -d)\nBIN=\"$APP/fxrates\"\nDATABASE_URL=\"$WORK/fxrates.db\"\nexport DATABASE_URL\nSERVER=\"\"\n\nstop_server() {\n    if [ -n \"$SERVER\" ]; then\n        pkill -TERM -P \"$SERVER\" 2>/dev/null\n        kill -TERM \"$SERVER\" 2>/dev/null\n        wait \"$SERVER\" 2>/dev/null\n        SERVER=\"\"\n    fi\n}\ntrap 'stop_server; rm -rf \"$WORK\"' EXIT\ntrap 'exit 1' INT TERM\n\nif [ ! -x \"$BIN\" ]; then\n    echo \"error: no executable ./fxrates at the application root $APP.\" >&2\n    echo \"The deliverable is an executable named fxrates at the application root.\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nPORT=$(python3 -c 'import socket; s = socket.socket(); s.bind((\"127.0.0.1\", 0)); print(s.getsockname()[1])')\nBASE=\"http://127.0.0.1:$PORT\"\n\nPASSED=0\nFAILED=0\n\npass() { PASSED=$((PASSED + 1)); echo \"PASS $1\"; }\nfail() { FAILED=$((FAILED + 1)); echo \"FAIL $1\"; }\n\n# check <id> <expected exit> <fxrates args...>  — expected standard output on stdin.\ncheck() {\n    id=$1\n    want_rc=$2\n    shift 2\n    cat > \"$WORK/want\"\n    (cd \"$APP\" && \"$BIN\" \"$@\") > \"$WORK/got\" 2> \"$WORK/err\" < /dev/null\n    rc=$?\n    if [ \"$rc\" -eq \"$want_rc\" ] && cmp -s \"$WORK/want\" \"$WORK/got\"; then\n        pass \"$id: fxrates $*\"\n    else\n        fail \"$id: fxrates $*\"\n        echo \"  exit: expected $want_rc, got $rc\"\n        diff \"$WORK/want\" \"$WORK/got\" | sed 's/^/  /'\n        sed 's/^/  stderr: /' \"$WORK/err\"\n    fi\n}\n\n# http <id> <expected status> <path>  — expected JSON body on stdin (compared only for 200).\nhttp() {\n    id=$1\n    want_status=$2\n    path=$3\n    cat > \"$WORK/want\"\n    if python3 - \"$BASE$path\" \"$want_status\" \"$WORK/want\" > \"$WORK/got\" 2>&1 <<'PY'\nimport json, sys, urllib.error, urllib.request\nurl, want, want_file = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2]), sys.argv[3]\ntry:\n    with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=15) as r:\n        status, body = r.status, r.read()\nexcept urllib.error.HTTPError as e:\n    status, body = e.code, e.read()\nexcept Exception as e:\n    print(f\"request failed: {e}\")\n    sys.exit(1)\nif status != want:\n    print(f\"status: expected {want}, got {status}\")\n    print(body.decode(\"utf-8\", \"replace\")[:400])\n    sys.exit(1)\nif want != 200:\n    sys.exit(0)\ntry:\n    got = json.loads(body)\nexcept ValueError:\n    print(\"body is not JSON:\", body.decode(\"utf-8\", \"replace\")[:400])\n    sys.exit(1)\nexpected = json.loads(open(want_file, encoding=\"utf-8\").read())\nif got != expected:\n    print(\"expected:\", json.dumps(expected, sort_keys=True))\n    print(\"got:     \", json.dumps(got, sort_keys=True))\n    sys.exit(1)\nPY\n    then\n        pass \"$id: GET $path\"\n    else\n        fail \"$id: GET $path\"\n        sed 's/^/  /' \"$WORK/got\"\n    fi\n}\n\n# start_server — run `fxrates serve` in the background and wait up to 30 s for /health.\nstart_server() {\n    (cd \"$APP\" && exec \"$BIN\" serve --port \"$PORT\") > \"$WORK/server.log\" 2>&1 < /dev/null &\n    SERVER=$!\n    tries=0\n    until python3 -c \"import urllib.request, sys; urllib.request.urlopen(sys.argv[1], timeout=2)\" \\\n            \"$BASE/health\" 2>/dev/null; do\n        tries=$((tries + 1))\n        if [ \"$tries\" -ge 30 ] || ! kill -0 \"$SERVER\" 2>/dev/null; then\n            echo \"FAIL S1: fxrates serve --port $PORT did not answer GET /health within 30 s\"\n            sed 's/^/  server: /' \"$WORK/server.log\"\n            echo \"FxRates: $PASSED passed, unscored HTTP checks (server did not start)\"\n            exit 1\n        fi\n        sleep 1\n    done\n}\n\n# Init owns schema creation for this new test store; never run a build or DDL here.\n# ── A. Do not filter, skip, or reinterpret.\n#\n# Runs ./fxrates against a fresh database initialized by the application.\n# Loads the supplied ECB files from the command line,\n# starts `./fxrates serve` on a free local port, and compares every command's exit code and\n# standard output, and every HTTP response's status and JSON body, with the known answer below.\n# JSON bodies are compared as values, so key order and whitespace do not matter. Standard error\n# and error-response bodies are never compared. No network beyond 127.0.0.1 is used.\n#\n#   sh sources/run.sh               from the application root (how `drydock uat` runs it)\n#   sh uat/FxRates/bin/run.sh APP   from anywhere, grading the application root APP\n#\n# Exit 0 only when every check passes.\nset -u\n\nHERE=$(cd \"$(dirname \"$0\")\" && pwd)\nAPP=$(cd \"${1:-.}\" && pwd)\nif [ -f \"$HERE/eurofxref-hist_2025-01.csv\" ]; then DATA=$HERE; else DATA=$(cd \"$HERE/../sources\" && pwd); fi\nWORK=$(mktemp -d)\nBIN=\"$APP/fxrates\"\nDATABASE_URL=\"$WORK/fxrates.db\"\nexport DATABASE_URL\nSERVER=\"\"\n\nstop_server() {\n    if [ -n \"$SERVER\" ]; then\n        pkill -TERM -P \"$SERVER\" 2>/dev/null\n        kill -TERM \"$SERVER\" 2>/dev/null\n        wait \"$SERVER\" 2>/dev/null\n        SERVER=\"\"\n    fi\n}\ntrap 'stop_server; rm -rf \"$WORK\"' EXIT\ntrap 'exit 1' INT TERM\n\nif [ ! -x \"$BIN\" ]; then\n    echo \"error: no executable ./fxrates at the application root $APP.\" >&2\n    echo \"The deliverable is an executable named fxrates at the application root.\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nPORT=$(python3 -c 'import socket; s = socket.socket(); s.bind((\"127.0.0.1\", 0)); print(s.getsockname()[1])')\nBASE=\"http://127.0.0.1:$PORT\"\n\nPASSED=0\nFAILED=0\n\npass() { PASSED=$((PASSED + 1)); echo \"PASS $1\"; }\nfail() { FAILED=$((FAILED + 1)); echo \"FAIL $1\"; }\n\n# check <id> <expected exit> <fxrates args...>  — expected standard output on stdin.\ncheck() {\n    id=$1\n    want_rc=$2\n    shift 2\n    cat > \"$WORK/want\"\n    (cd \"$APP\" && \"$BIN\" \"$@\") > \"$WORK/got\" 2> \"$WORK/err\" < /dev/null\n    rc=$?\n    if [ \"$rc\" -eq \"$want_rc\" ] && cmp -s \"$WORK/want\" \"$WORK/got\"; then\n        pass \"$id: fxrates $*\"\n    else\n        fail \"$id: fxrates $*\"\n        echo \"  exit: expected $want_rc, got $rc\"\n        diff \"$WORK/want\" \"$WORK/got\" | sed 's/^/  /'\n        sed 's/^/  stderr: /' \"$WORK/err\"\n    fi\n}\n\n# http <id> <expected status> <path>  — expected JSON body on stdin (compared only for 200).\nhttp() {\n    id=$1\n    want_status=$2\n    path=$3\n    cat > \"$WORK/want\"\n    if python3 - \"$BASE$path\" \"$want_status\" \"$WORK/want\" > \"$WORK/got\" 2>&1 <<'PY'\nimport json, sys, urllib.error, urllib.request\nurl, want, want_file = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2]), sys.argv[3]\ntry:\n    with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=15) as r:\n        status, body = r.status, r.read()\nexcept urllib.error.HTTPError as e:\n    status, body = e.code, e.read()\nexcept Exception as e:\n    print(f\"request failed: {e}\")\n    sys.exit(1)\nif status != want:\n    print(f\"status: expected {want}, got {status}\")\n    print(body.decode(\"utf-8\", \"replace\")[:400])\n    sys.exit(1)\nif want != 200:\n    sys.exit(0)\ntry:\n    got = json.loads(body)\nexcept ValueError:\n    print(\"body is not JSON:\", body.decode(\"utf-8\", \"replace\")[:400])\n    sys.exit(1)\nexpected = json.loads(open(want_file, encoding=\"utf-8\").read())\nif got != expected:\n    print(\"expected:\", json.dumps(expected, sort_keys=True))\n    print(\"got:     \", json.dumps(got, sort_keys=True))\n    sys.exit(1)\nPY\n    then\n        pass \"$id: GET $path\"\n    else\n        fail \"$id: GET $path\"\n        sed 's/^/  /' \"$WORK/got\"\n    fi\n}\n\n# start_server — run `fxrates serve` in the background and wait up to 30 s for /health.\nstart_server() {\n    (cd \"$APP\" && exec \"$BIN\" serve --port \"$PORT\") > \"$WORK/server.log\" 2>&1 < /dev/null &\n    SERVER=$!\n    tries=0\n    until python3 -c \"import urllib.request, sys; urllib.request.urlopen(sys.argv[1], timeout=2)\" \\\n            \"$BASE/health\" 2>/dev/null; do\n        tries=$((tries + 1))\n        if [ \"$tries\" -ge 30 ] || ! kill -0 \"$SERVER\" 2>/dev/null; then\n            echo \"FAIL S1: fxrates serve --port $PORT did not answer GET /health within 30 s\"\n            sed 's/^/  server: /' \"$WORK/server.log\"\n            echo \"FxRates: $PASSED passed, unscored HTTP checks (server did not start)\"\n            exit 1\n        fi\n        sleep 1\n    done\n}\n\n# Init owns schema creation for this new test store; {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_011mGecVAnZbX9pM45CJp9tM","type":"tool_result","content":"=== cli/dispatch.py\n\"\"\"Command resolution and the mapping from raised errors to exit codes.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport importlib\nimport re\nimport sys\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Sequence\n\nfrom cli.errors import OperationalError, RejectedFile, UsageError\n\nCOMMAND_PACKAGE = \"cli.commands\"\n_COMMAND_NAME = re.compile(r\"[a-z][a-z0-9_]*\")\n_MAPPED_ERRORS = (OperationalError, UsageError, RejectedFile)\n\nHandler = Callable[[list[str]], int]\n\n\ndef execute(handler: Handler, args: Sequence[str]) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Call handler(args) and return its result; map a raised expected error to its exit code.\n\n    The error's message goes to stderr as one line. Nothing is written to stdout on failure.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        return handler(list(args))\n    except _MAPPED_ERRORS as exc:\n        message = \" \".join(str(exc).split())\n        print(f\"error: {message}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return exc.exit_code\n\n\ndef resolve(name: str) -> Handler:\n    \"\"\"Return the run() of the cli.commands module named by the first argument.\"\"\"\n    if not _COMMAND_NAME.fullmatch(name):\n        raise UsageError(f\"unknown command {name!r}\")\n    module_name = f\"{COMMAND_PACKAGE}.{name}\"\n    try:\n        module = importlib.import_module(module_name)\n    except ModuleNotFoundError as exc:\n        # Only a missing command module is a usage error; a broken import inside one propagates.\n        if exc.name == module_name:\n            raise UsageError(f\"unknown command {name!r}\") from None\n        raise\n    return module.run\n\n\ndef dispatch(argv: Sequence[str]) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Route argv to its command module and return the exit code.\"\"\"\n\n    def route(args: list[str]) -> int:\n        if not args:\n            raise UsageError(\"no command given\")\n        return resolve(args[0])(args[1:])\n\n    return execute(route, argv)\n\n=== cli/errors.py\n\"\"\"Expected failures a command raises. Each class carries the exit code the dispatcher returns.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass OperationalError(Exception):\n    \"\"\"The command ran but could not complete its work.\"\"\"\n\n    exit_code = 1\n\n\nclass UsageError(Exception):\n    \"\"\"The command line was not a valid invocation.\"\"\"\n\n    exit_code = 2\n\n\nclass RejectedFile(Exception):\n    \"\"\"An input file was refused before any of its content was written.\"\"\"\n\n    exit_code = 3\n\n=== cli/testing.py\n\"\"\"In-process command runner for tests: no subprocess, output captured.\"\"\"\n\nimport contextlib\nimport io\n\nfrom cli import main\n\n\ndef cli_runner(*args: str) -> tuple[int, str, str]:\n    \"\"\"Return (exit_code, stdout, stderr) without spawning a process.\"\"\"\n    out, err = io.StringIO(), io.StringIO()\n    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(out), contextlib.redirect_stderr(err):\n        code = main(list(args))\n    return code, out.getvalue(), err.getvalue()\n\n=== cli/commands/__init__.py\n\"\"\"Command modules. Each module named for a command exposes run(args: list[str]) -> int.\"\"\"\n\n=== config.py\n\"\"\"Runtime configuration resolved from the environment.\n\nThis module is the one configuration boundary. An unset or empty variable is skipped.\n    \"\"\"\n    url = _environment_value(DATABASE_URL_ENV)\n    if url.startswith(SQLITE_URL_PREFIX):\n        url = url[len(SQLITE_URL_PREFIX):]\n    if url:\n        return Path(url)\n\n    path = _environment_value(DATABASE_PATH_ENV)\n    if path:\n        return Path(path)\n\n    return Path(DEFAULT_DATABASE_PATH)\n\n=== conftest.py\n\"\"\"Shared pytest fixtures for the CLI and web foundations.\"\"\"\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom app_server import testing as web_testing\nfrom cli import testing as cli_testing\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef cli_runner():\n    return cli_testing.cli_runner\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef web_client():\n    return web_testing.web_client()\n\n=== fxrates\n#!/bin/sh\n# Application entry point. methods one table grants, bound from the declaration rather than defined by hand.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, table: Table, operations: Iterable[Operation], database: Database) -> None:\n {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01HjY7N1wFB12L4UaXvKFseB","type":"tool_result","content":"    finally:\n        database.close()\n\n\n@contextmanager\ndef db_session():\n    \"\"\"Share this connection with the feature; always roll back, never provision schema.\n\n    Under the acceptance harness the rollback is the harness's, at the end of the criterion, so\n    a request made after this block still sees the setup.\n    \"\"\"\n    with committed_session() as database:\n        with database.rollback_session():\n            yield database\n=== db.py\n\"\"\"Persistence access for a Drydock Target.\n\nThis file is shipped by Drydock and copied into the build unchanged. Do not edit it here: edit\n``DATABASE.md`` and rebuild. It is hardened and tested once, in Drydock's own suite, so every\nTarget inherits a persistence layer that has already passed rather than one re-derived from prose\non each build.\n\nThe application-facing surface is ``Database``. One attribute per declared table, one method per\ndeclared access pattern::\n\n    db = Database(dsn, SCHEMA)\n    ticket = db.tickets.get(id=7)\n    open_tickets = db.tickets.list(status=\"open\")\n\n``schema.py`` beside this file is generated from ``DATABASE.md`` and carries the tables, the\noperations, and the row types. It contains no SQL. Statements are constructed here, by the driver\nfor the engine in use, so a parameter placeholder never appears in generated code or in a caller.\n\nValues reach the database as bound parameters, never as formatted text. Identifiers cannot be\nbound in any engine, so they are taken only from the generated schema — which Drydock validated\nagainst ``^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`` before emitting it — and are quoted on the way out.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable, Mapping, Sequence\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, fields\nfrom contextlib import contextmanager, nullcontext\nimport threading\nfrom typing import Any\n\n__all__ = [\n    \"Database\",\n    \"Driver\",\n    \"Operation\",\n    \"PersistenceError\",\n    \"Schema\",\n    \"Table\",\n    \"statements\",\n    \"UnknownOperation\",\n    \"begin_acceptance_transaction\",\n    \"end_acceptance_transaction\",\n]\n\nVERBS = (\"get\", \"list\", \"create\", \"update\", \"delete\")\n#: The comparisons a declared Match term may state; anything else is refused before SQL is built.\nCOMPARISONS = (\"=\", \"<\", \"<=\", \">\", \">=\")\nDIRECTIONS = (\"asc\", \"desc\")\n\n\nclass PersistenceError(RuntimeError):\n    \"\"\"A persistence failure the caller may act on, raised in place of a driver exception.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass UnknownOperation(PersistenceError):\n    \"\"\"A verb was requested that the declaration does not grant for that table.\"\"\"\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Table:\n    \"\"\"One declared table: its columns and the column that identifies a row.\"\"\"\n\n    name: str\n    columns: tuple[str, ...]\n    primary_key: str | None = None\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Operation:\n    \"\"\"One declared access pattern, reduced to what executing it requires.\n\n    ``name`` is the method callers use and ``verb`` is its Kind, how it runs; a name that is a\n    verb runs as that verb. ``inputs`` are the parameters the caller supplies. ``match`` is the\n    equality predicate of a ``get``, ``update``, ``upsert``, or ``delete``, every field of it\n    required; a ``list`` filters on whichever inputs are supplied, and the inputs of a\n    ``create``, ``update``, or ``upsert`` outside ``match`` are the values written. ``row`` is the dataclass the operation returns, and\n    ``columns`` are its fields; an operation with no ``row`` returns a count. ``compare`` holds\n    ``(field, op, column)`` for each input compared other than by equality with its own column,\n    such as ``(\"start_date\", \">=\", \"date\")``, and ``order`` the ``(column, direction)`` sort keys\n    of a ``list``.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    identifier: str\n    table: str\n    verb: str\n    inputs: tuple[str, ...]\n    row: type | None = None\n    columns: tuple[str, ...] = ()\n    match: tuple[str, ...] = ()\n    name: str = \"\"\n    compare: tuple[tuple[str, str, str], ...] = ()\n    order: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] = ()\n\n    def keys(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:\n        \"\"\"The match fields compared by equality: what reads back the one row a write reached.\"\"\"\n        compared = {field for field, op, _ in self.compare if op != \"=\"}\n        return tuple(name for name in self.match if name not in compared)\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Schema:\n    \"\"\"The generated declaration: every table and every operation reaching one.\"\"\"\n\n    tables: tuple[Table, ...]\n    operations: tuple[Operation, ...]\n\n    def by_table(self) -> dict[str, tuple[Operation, ...]]:\n        grouped: dict[str, list[Operation]] = {table.name: [] for table in self.tables}\n        for operation in self.operations:\n            grouped.setdefault(operation.table, []).append(operation)\n        return {name: tuple(items) for name, items in grouped.items()}\n\n\nclass Driver:\n    \"\"\"Statement construction shared by every engine.\n\n    Subclasses supply connection handling and the two things engines genuinely disagree about:\n    how a parameter is spelled, and how a freshly inserted row reports its key. Everything else is\n    identical SQL, so it is written once here rather than twice in the engines.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def prepare_schema(self, sql: str) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Translate generated DDL for this engine.\"\"\"\n        return sql\n\n    #: Spelled by the DB-API driver, not by this class's callers.\n    paramstyle = \"qmark\"\n    returning = False\n\n    def connect(self) -> Any:  # pragma: no cover - engine specific\n        raise NotImplementedError\n\n    def pin(self) -> Any:  # pragma: no cover - engine specific\n        \"\"\"Serve one connection to every thread until ``close``. The acceptance harness's.\"\"\"\n        raise NotImplementedError\n\n    def identity(self) -> str:  # pragma: no cover - engine specific\n        \"\"\"Name the store, so two spellings of one DSN share one acceptance transaction.\"\"\"\n        raise NotImplementedError\n\n    def close(self) -> None:  # pragma: no cover - engine specific\n        raise NotImplementedError\n\n    def placeholder(self, index: int) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Render parameter ``index`` (0-based) in this engine's spelling.\"\"\"\n        return \"?\" if self.paramstyle == \"qmark\" else \"%s\"\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def quote(identifier: str) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Quote a declared identifier. Never called with caller-supplied text.\"\"\"\n        if not identifier.replace(\"_\", \"\").isalnum():\n            raise PersistenceError(f\"refusing unsafe identifier {identifier!r}\")\n        return f'\"{identifier}\"'\n\n    def _predicate(\n        self, names: Sequence[str], start: int = 0, compare: Sequence[tuple[str, str, str]] = ()\n    ) -> str:\n        \"\"\"``names`` are input fields; each is compared with its declared column, else its own.\"\"\"\n        by_field = {field: (op, column) for field, op, column in compare}\n        terms = []\n        for offset, name in enumerate(names):\n            op, column = by_field.get(name, (\"=\", name))\n            if op not in COMPARISONS:\n                raise PersistenceError(f\"refusing undeclared comparison {op!r}\")\n            terms.append(f\"{self.quote(column)} {op} {self.placeholder(start + offset)}\")\n        return \" AND \".join(terms)\n\n    def select(\n        self,\n        table: str,\n        columns: Sequence[str],\n        predicate: Sequence[str],\n        compare: Sequence[tuple[str, str, str]] = (),\n        order: Sequence[tuple[str, str]] = (),\n    ) -> str:\n        selected = \", \".join(self.quote(name) for name in columns)\n        statement = f\"SELECT {selected} FROM {self.quote(table)}\"\n        if predicate:\n            statement += f\" WHERE {self._predicate(predicate, 0, compare)}\"\n        if order:\n            for _, direction in order:\n                if direction not in DIRECTIONS:\n                    raise PersistenceError(f\"refusing undeclared order {direction!r}\")\n            keys = \", \".join(\n                f\"{self.quote(column)} {direction.upper()}\" for column, direction in order\n            )\n            statement += f\" ORDER BY {keys}\"\n        return statement\n\n    def insert(self, table: str, columns: Sequence[str], key: str | None) -> str:\n        names = \", \".join(self.quote(name) for name in columns)\n        marks = \", \".join(self.placeholder(index) for index in range(len(columns)))\n        statement = f\"INSERT INTO {self.quote(table)} ({names}) VALUES ({marks})\"\n        if self.returning and key:\n            statement += f\" RETURNING {self.quote(key)}\"\n        return statement\n\n    def update(\n        self,\n        table: str,\n        columns: Sequence[str],\n        predicate: Sequence[str],\n        compare: Sequence[tuple[str, str, str]] = (),\n    ) -> str:\n        assignments = \", \".join(\n            f\"{self.quote(name)} = {self.placeholder(index)}\" for index, name in enumerate(columns)\n        )\n        statement = f\"UPDATE {self.quote(table)} SET {assignments}\"\n        if predicate:\n            statement += f\" WHERE {self._predicate(predicate, len(columns), compare)}\"\n        return statement\n\n    def upsert(self, table: str, columns: Sequence[str], match: Sequence[str]) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Insert a row, or replace the Set columns of the row ``match`` identifies.\n\n        ``match`` names a declared unique key, which is what ``ON CONFLICT`` requires; SQLite\n        and PostgreSQL spell the statement identically.\n        \"\"\"\n        assigned = [name for name in columns if name not in match]\n        target = \", \".join(self.quote(name) for name in match)\n        action = (\n            \"DO UPDATE SET \"\n            + \", \".join(f\"{self.quote(name)} = excluded.{self.quote(name)}\" for name in assigned)\n            if assigned\n            else \"DO NOTHING\"\n        )\n        return f\"{self.insert(table, columns, None)} ON CONFLICT ({target}) {action}\"\n\n    def delete(\n        self, table: str, predicate: Sequence[str], compare: Sequence[tuple[str, str, str]] = ()\n    ) -> str:\n        statement = f\"DELETE FROM {self.quote(table)}\"\n        if predicate:\n            statement += f\" WHERE {self._predicate(predicate, 0, compare)}\"\n        return statement\n\n    def inserted_key(self, cursor: Any) -> Any:  # pragma: no cover - engine specific\n        raise NotImplementedError\n\n\nclass TableAccess:\n    \"\"\"The methods one table grants, bound from the declaration rather than defined by hand.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, table: Table, operations: Iterable[Operation], database: Database) -> None:\n        self._table = table\n        self._database = database\n        self._operations = {operation.name or operation.verb: operation for operation in operations}\n\n    def __repr__(self) -> str:\n        granted = \", \".join(sorted(self._operations))\n        return f\"<TableAccess {self._table.name}: {granted or 'no declared operation'}>\"\n\n    def __getattr__(self, name: str) -> Callable[..., Any]:\n        operation = self._operations.get(name)\n        if operation is None:\n            granted = \", \".join(sorted(self._operations)) or \"none\"\n            raise UnknownOperation(\n                f\"{self._table.name} declares no {name!r} operation. Declared: {granted}. \"\n                \"Add an access pattern to DATABASE.md rather than reaching around this class.\"\n            )\n        return lambda **arguments: self._database.run(operation, arguments)\n\n\nclass _AcceptanceTransaction:\n    \"\"\"One transaction per store, shared by every ``Database`` this process opens; never committed.\n\n    The acceptance harness begins it before a criterion runs and rolls it back when the criterion\n    ends. The criterion's fixture, the application behind an in-process HTTP client, and an\n    in-process command all join it, so setup, behavior and readback see one another's writes and\n    none of them persists. Sequence[tuple[str, str, str]] = ()\n    ) -> str:\n        statement = f\"DELETE FROM {self.quote(table)}\"\n        if predicate:\n            statement += f\" WHERE {self._predicate(predicate, 0, compare)}\"\n        return statement\n\n    def inserted_key(self, cursor: Any) -> Any:  # pragma: no cover - engine specific\n        raise NotImplementedError\n\n\nclass TableAccess:\n    \"\"\"The methods one table grants, bound from the declaration rather than defined by hand.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, table: Table, operations: Iterable[Operation], database: Database) -> None:\n        self._table = table\n        self._database = database\n        self._operations = {operation.name or operation.verb: operation for operation in operations}\n\n    def __repr__(self) -> str:\n        granted = \", \".join(sorted(self._operations))\n        return f\"<TableAccess {self._table.name}: {granted or 'no declared operation'}>\"\n\n    def __getattr__(self, name: str) -> Callable[..., Any]:\n        operation = self._operations.get(name)\n        if operation is None:\n            granted = \", \".join(sorted(self._operations)) or \"none\"\n            raise UnknownOperation(\n                f\"{self._table.name} declares no {name!r} operation. Declared: {granted}. \"\n                \"Add an access pattern to DATABASE.md rather than reaching around this class.\"\n            )\n        return lambda **arguments: self._database.run(operation, arguments)\n\n\nclass _AcceptanceTransaction:\n    \"\"\"One transaction per store, shared by every ``Database`` this process opens; never committed.\n\n    The acceptance harness begins it before a criterion runs and rolls it back when the criterion\n    ends. The criterion's fixture, the application behind an in-process HTTP client, and an\n    in-process command all join it, so setup, behavior and readback see one another's writes and\n    none of them persists. A crash loses nothing: an engine discards an uncommitted transaction.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self) -> None:\n        self.lock = threading.RLock()\n        self._drivers: dict[str, Driver] = {}\n\n    def join(self, driver: Driver) -> Driver:\n        with self.lock:\n            shared = self._drivers.get(driver.identity())\n            if shared is None:\n                cursor = driver.pin().cursor()\n                try:\n                    cursor.execute(\"BEGIN\")\n                finally:\n                    cursor.close()\n                shared = self._drivers[driver.identity()] = driver\n            return shared\n\n    def rollback(self) -> None:\n        failures = []\n        with self.lock:\n            for identity, driver in self._drivers.items():\n                try:\n                    cursor = driver.pin().cursor()\n                    try:\n                        cursor.execute(\"ROLLBACK\")\n                    finally:\n                        cursor.close()\n                except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - every store is still closed\n                    failures.append(f\"{identity}: {exc}\")\n                finally:\n                    driver.close()\n            self._drivers.clear()\n        if failures:\n            raise PersistenceError(\"acceptance rollback failed: \" + \"; \".join(failures))\n\n\n_harness: _AcceptanceTransaction | None = None\n\n\ndef begin_acceptance_transaction() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Join every store this process opens from now on to one transaction the harness owns.\"\"\"\n    global _harness\n    if _harness is None:\n        _harness = _AcceptanceTransaction()\n\n\ndef end_acceptance_transaction() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Roll back the harness's transaction on every store it joined.\"\"\"\n    global _harness\n    harness, _harness = _harness, None\n    if harness is not None:\n        harness.rollback()\n\n\nclass Database:\n    \"\"\"One store, presented to callers as declared tables with declared methods.\n\n    Callers construct one instance, share it freely, and call methods synchronously. Connection\n    handling is internal and may change without affecting any caller.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, dsn: str, schema: Schema, *, driver: Driver | None = None) -> None:\n        self._rollback_owner = None\n        self._schema = schema\n        driver = driver if driver is not None else open_driver(dsn)\n        self._harness = _harness\n        self._driver = self._harness.join(driver) if self._harness is not None else driver\n        grouped = schema.by_table()\n        for table in schema.tables:\n            setattr(self, table.name, TableAccess(table, grouped.get(table.name, ()), self))\n\n    @property\n    def driver(self) -> Driver:\n        if self._harness is not None:\n            raise PersistenceError(\"driver access is forbidden inside the acceptance transaction\")\n        if self._rollback_owner is not None:\n            raise PersistenceError(\"driver access is forbidden inside a rollback session\")\n        return self._driver\n\n    def close(self) -> None:\n        if self._harness is not None:\n            return  # the acceptance harness owns the shared connection\n        if self._rollback_owner is not None:\n            raise PersistenceError(\"the rollback session owns connection lifetime\")\n        self._driver.close()\n\n    @contextmanager\n    def rollback_session(self):\n        \"\"\"Use this connection for setup, behavior and assertions; always roll back.\n\n        Normal calls remain autocommitted. No schema creation, nested transaction,\n        driver escape, or cross-thread operation is allowed in this scope. Under the acceptance\n        harness the scope is the harness's transaction, rolled back when the criterion ends, so\n        leaving it rolls nothing back.\n        \"\"\"\n        if self._harness is not None:\n            yield self\n            return\n        if self._rollback_owner is not None:\n            raise PersistenceError(\"nested rollback session\")\n        connection = self._driver.connect()\n        cursor = connection.cursor()\n        try:\n            cursor.execute(\"BEGIN\")\n            self._rollback_owner = threading.get_ident()\n            try:\n                yield self\n            finally:\n                try:\n                    cursor.execute(\"ROLLBACK\")\n                except Exception as exc:\n                    raise PersistenceError(f\"acceptance rollback failed: {exc}\") from exc\n                finally:\n                    self._rollback_owner = None\n        finally:\n            cursor.close()\n            self._driver.close()\n\n    def __enter__(self) -> Database:\n        return self\n\n    def __exit__(self, *_: object) -> None:\n        self.close()\n\n    def _initialize_schema(self, sql: str) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Apply generated idempotent creation DDL, including inside harness rollback.\n\n        Only the generated initializer calls this path. Ordinary execute_script remains\n        forbidden in rollback sessions; initialization never accepts data or migration SQL.\n        \"\"\"\n        prepared = statements(self._driver.prepare_schema(sql))\n        for statement in prepared:\n            words = statement.upper().split()\n            if words[:5] not in (\n                [\"CREATE\", \"TABLE\", \"IF\", \"NOT\", \"EXISTS\"],\n                [\"CREATE\", \"INDEX\", \"IF\", \"NOT\", \"EXISTS\"],\n            ):\n                raise PersistenceError(\"initialization permits only idempotent table/index creation\")\n        with self._harness.lock if self._harness is not None else nullcontext():\n            cursor = self._open(\"initialization\")\n            try:\n                for statement in prepared:\n                    cursor.execute(statement)\n            finally:\n                cursor.close()\n\n    def execute_script(self, sql: str) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Apply owner-supplied DDL outside rollback sessions; explicit init uses generated creation DDL.\"\"\"\n        if self._rollback_owner is not None or self._harness is not None:\n            raise PersistenceError(\"schema and transaction SQL are forbidden in rollback sessions\")\n        cursor = self._open(\"schema\")\n        try:\n            for statement in statements(self._driver.prepare_schema(sql)):\n                cursor.execute(statement)\n        finally:\n            cursor.close()\n\n    def run(self, operation: Operation, arguments: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Any:\n        \"\"\"Execute one declared operation with bound parameters.\"\"\"\n        unknown = sorted(set(arguments) - set(operation.inputs))\n        if unknown:\n            raise PersistenceError(\n                f\"{operation.identifier} does not accept {', '.join(unknown)}. Declared inputs: \"\n                f\"{', '.join(operation.inputs) or 'none'}.\"\n            )\n        if operation not in self._schema.operations:\n            raise UnknownOperation(f\"{operation.identifier} is not a declared operation\")\n        missing = [name for name in self._match(operation) if name not in arguments]\n        if missing:\n            raise PersistenceError(f\"{operation.identifier} requires {', '.join(missing)}\")\n        if operation.verb == \"delete\" and not arguments:\n            raise PersistenceError(f\"{operation.identifier} requires a delete predicate\")\n        names = [name for name in operation.inputs if name in arguments]\n        values = [arguments[name] for name in names]\n        # The harness's one connection serves the criterion and the application's request\n        # threads alike, so an operation holds it for its whole statement and savepoint.\n        with self._harness.lock if self._harness is not None else nullcontext():\n            scoped = self._rollback_owner is not None or self._harness is not None\n            cursor = self._open(operation.identifier)\n            try:\n                if scoped:\n                    cursor.execute(\"SAVEPOINT drydock_operation\")\n                result = self._dispatch(operation, cursor, names, values)\n                if scoped:\n                    cursor.execute(\"RELEASE SAVEPOINT drydock_operation\")\n                return result\n            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - translated at the boundary on purpose\n                if scoped:\n                    cursor.execute(\"ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT drydock_operation\")\n                    cursor.execute(\"RELEASE SAVEPOINT drydock_operation\")\n                raise PersistenceError(f\"{operation.identifier} failed: {exc}\") from exc\n            finally:\n                cursor.close()\n\n    def _open(self, action: str) -> Any:\n        \"\"\"Return a cursor, translating a refused or failed connection.\"\"\"\n        if self._rollback_owner not in (None, threading.get_ident()):\n            raise PersistenceError(\"rollback session requires its owning thread and connection\")\n        try:\n            return self._driver.connect().cursor()\n        except PersistenceError:\n            raise\n        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - translated at the boundary on purpose\n            raise PersistenceError(f\"{action} could not connect: {exc}\") from exc\n\n    def _dispatch(\n        self,\n        operation: Operation,\n        cursor: Any,\n        names: list[str],\n        values: list[Any],\n    ) -> Any:\n        verb = operation.verb\n        table = operation.table\n        match = self._match(operation)\n        if verb in (\"get\", \"list\"):\n            columns = operation.columns or self._columns(table)\n            statement = self._driver.select(\n                table, columns, names, operation.compare, operation.order\n            )\n            cursor.execute(statement, values)\n            rows = cursor.fetchall() if verb == \"list\" else cursor.fetchmany(1)\n            built = [self._build(operation, columns, row) for row in rows]\n            return built if verb == \"list\" else (built[0] if built else None)\n        if verb == \"create\":\n            key = self._primary_key(table)\n            cursor.execute(self._driver.insert(table, names, key), values)\n            identity = self._driver.inserted_key(cursor)\n            if operation.row is None:\n                return identity\n            # The declared Output row, read back so column defaults are included. A supplied key\n            # wins over the engine's report: SQLite's lastrowid is the rowid, not a text key.\n            if key is None:\n                return self._build(operation, names, values)\n            if key in names:\n                identity = values[names.index(key)]\n            columns = operation.columns or self._columns(table)\n            cursor.execute(self._driver.select(table, columns, [key]), [identity])\n            return self._build(operation, columns, cursor.fetchone())\n        if verb == \"update\":\n            if not match:\n                raise PersistenceError(f\"{operation.identifier} updates {table} without a match\")\n            assigned = [name for name in names if name not in match]\n            if not assigned:\n                raise PersistenceError(f\"{operation.identifier} supplies no column to set\")\n            keys = [values[names.index(name)] for name in match]\n            ordered = [values[names.index(name)] for name in assigned] + keys\n            cursor.execute(self._driver.update(table, assigned, match, operation.compare), ordered)\n            if operation.row is None:\n                return cursor.rowcount\n            if not cursor.rowcount:\n                return None\n            # The declared Output row, read back by its equality match so unassigned columns are\n            # included; a row-returning update matches a unique key by equality.\n            columns = operation.columns or self._columns(table)\n            equal = operation.keys() if operation.match else match\n            cursor.execute(\n                self._driver.select(table, columns, equal, operation.compare),\n                [values[names.index(name)] for name in equal],\n            )\n            return self._build(operation, columns, cursor.fetchone())\n        if verb == \"upsert\":\n            cursor.execute(self._driver.upsert(table, names, match), values)\n            if operation.row is None:\n                return cursor.rowcount\n            columns = operation.columns or self._columns(table)\n            keys = [values[names.index(name)] for name in match]\n            cursor.execute(self._driver.select(table, columns, match), keys)\n            return self._build(operation, columns, cursor.fetchone())\n        if verb == \"delete\":\n            cursor.execute(self._driver.delete(table, names, operation.compare), values)\n            if operation.row is None:\n                return cursor.rowcount\n            # The declared Output, built from the key it was given; None when nothing matched.\n            return self._build(operation, names, values) if cursor.rowcount else None\n        raise UnknownOperation(f\"{operation.identifier} names unsupported verb {verb!r}\")\n\n    def _columns(self, table: str) -> tuple[str, ...]:\n        for declared in self._schema.tables:\n            if declared.name == table:\n                return declared.columns\n        raise PersistenceError(f\"{table} is not a declared table\")\n\n    def _match(self, operation: Operation) -> tuple[str, ...]:\n        \"\"\"The required equality predicate; a schema generated without one keys by the PK.\"\"\"\n        if operation.match or operation.verb not in (\"get\", \"update\", \"delete\"):\n            return operation.match\n        key = self._primary_key(operation.table)\n        if key and (operation.verb == \"update\" or key in operation.inputs):\n            return (key,)\n        return ()\n\n    def _primary_key(self, table: str) -> str | None:\n        for declared in self._schema.tables:\n            if declared.name == table:\n                return declared.primary_key\n        return None\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def _build(operation: Operation, columns: Sequence[str], row: Sequence[Any]) -> Any:\n        if operation.row is None:\n            return dict(zip(columns, row, strict=False))\n        accepted = {field.name for field in fields(operation.row)}\n        return operation.row(**{\n            name: value for name, value in zip(columns, row, strict=False) if name in accepted\n        })\n\n\ndef statements(sql: str) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Split a DDL script into statements.\n\n    Comment lines are dropped and a semicolon inside a quoted literal does not end a statement —\n    a ``DEFAULT \\'a;b\\'`` would otherwise be cut in half, and the halves are not valid SQL.\n    \"\"\"\n    body = \"\\n\".join(line for line in sql.splitlines() if not line.lstrip().startswith(\"--\"))\n    parts: list[str] = []\n    current: list[str] = []\n    quoted = False\n    for character in body:\n        if character == \"'\":\n            quoted = not quoted\n        if character == \";\" and not quoted:\n            parts.append(\"\".join(current))\n            current = []\n            continue\n        current.append(character)\n    parts.append(\"\".join(current))\n    return [statement.strip() for statement in parts if statement.strip()]\n\n\ndef open_driver(dsn: str) -> Driver:\n    \"\"\"Select the engine from the DSN, so one build serves SQLite in test and Postgres in production.\"\"\"\n    scheme = dsn.split(\"://\", 1)[0].lower() if \"://\" in dsn else \"sqlite\"\n    if scheme in (\"postgres\", \"postgresql\"):\n        try:\n            from .postgres import PostgresDriver\n        except ImportError:  # flat layout\n            from postgres import PostgresDriver\n\n        return PostgresDriver(dsn)\n    if scheme in (\"sqlite\", \"file\") or \"://\" not in dsn:\n        try:\n            from .sqlite import SqliteDriver\n        except ImportError:  # flat layout\n Drydock ships sqlite and postgres; add a driver \"\n        \"beside this file and a branch here for another engine.\"\n    )\n=== schema.sql\n-- Generated by Drydock from DATABASE.md. Edit the declaration, not this file.\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS \"rates\" (\"id\" INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, \"date\" TEXT NOT NULL, \"currency\" TEXT NOT NULL, \"rate\" TEXT NOT NULL, UNIQUE (\"date\", \"currency\"));\nCREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS \"rates_date_idx\" ON \"rates\" (\"date\");\nCREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS \"rates_currency_date_idx\" ON \"rates\" (\"currency\", \"date\");\n=== pyproject\n[project]\nname = \"fxrates\"\nversion = \"0.1.0\"\nrequires-python = \">=3.11\"\ndependencies = [\n    \"fastapi>=0.162.0\",\n    \"httpx2>=2.16.0\",\n    \"pytest>=9.1.1\",\n    \"uvicorn>=0.54.0\",\n]\n\n[tool.pytest.ini_options]\ntestpaths = [\"tests\"]\npythonpath = [\".\"]\n=== test.sh\n#!/bin/sh\n# CommandCenter Operation\n# Name: Run Test Suite\n# Type: batch\n\n# Runs the project test suite (pytest -q) from the application root in the\n# project .venv. Every\nviolation raises UsageError, which the dispatcher maps to exit status 2 with nothing on stdout.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Sequence\n\nfrom cli.errors import UsageError\n\nDEFAULT_PORT = 8000\n_INTEGER = re.compile(r\"-?[0-9]+\")\n\nRule = Callable[[str, list[str]], list[str | int]]\n\n\ndef parse(argv: Sequence[str]) -> tuple[str, list[str | int]]:\n    \"\"\"Validate argv and return (command name, parsed arguments); raise UsageError on a violation.\"\"\"\n    if not argv:\n        raise UsageError(\"no command given\")\n    name, rest = argv[0], list(argv[1:])\n    rule = _RULES.get(name)\n    if rule is None:\n        # A name outside the declared table is valid only when a command module provides it.\n        # Imported here because cli.dispatch imports this module.\n        from cli.dispatch import resolve\n\n        resolve(name)\n        return name, rest\n    return name, rule(name, rest)\n\n\ndef _no_arguments(name: str, rest: list[str]) -> list[str | int]:\n    if rest:\n        raise UsageError(f\"{name} takes no arguments\")\n    return []\n\n\ndef _load(name: str, rest: list[str]) -> list[str | int]:\n    if any(arg.startswith(\"-\") for arg in rest):\n        raise UsageError(f\"{name} has an unknown option\")\n    if len(rest) != 1:\n        raise UsageError(f\"{name} takes exactly one path\")\n    return [rest[0]]\n\n\ndef _serve(name: str, rest: list[str]) -> list[str | int]:\n    if not rest:\n        return [DEFAULT_PORT]\n    if len(rest) != 2 or rest[0] != \"--port\":\n        raise UsageError(f\"{name} accepts only --port <n>\")\n    if not _INTEGER.fullmatch(rest[1]):\n        raise UsageError(f\"--port value {rest[1]!r} is not an integer\")\n    return [int(rest[1])]\n\n\n_RULES: dict[str, Rule] = {\n    \"init\": _no_arguments,\n    \"fetch\": _no_arguments,\n    \"load\": _load,\n    \"serve\": _serve,\n}\n"}}}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_014axaQLx2fEHv4jLXi5iXT5","type":"tool_result","content":"The file /mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/FxRates/runs/20261027.190646/build/FxRates/cli/dispatch.py has been updated successfully."}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"a9cb209c-cf78-4d6a-b621-670bbb8c6b3d","uuid":"db8404da-ea43-4ea7-b976-0d57cadd186d","timestamp":"2026-10-27T19:34:31.600Z","tool_use_result":{"filePath":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/FxRates/runs/20261027.190646/build/FxRates/cli/dispatch.py","oldString":"from cli.errors import OperationalError, RejectedFile, UsageError\n\nCOMMAND_PACKAGE","newString":"from cli.errors import OperationalError, RejectedFile, UsageError\nfrom cli.usage import parse\n\nCOMMAND_PACKAGE","originalFile":"\"\"\"Command resolution and the mapping from raised errors to exit codes.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport importlib\nimport re\nimport sys\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Sequence\n\nfrom cli.errors import OperationalError, RejectedFile, UsageError\n\nCOMMAND_PACKAGE = \"cli.commands\"\n_COMMAND_NAME = re.compile(r\"[a-z][a-z0-9_]*\")\n_MAPPED_ERRORS = (OperationalError, UsageError, RejectedFile)\n\nHandler = Callable[[list[str]], int]\n\n\ndef execute(handler: Handler, args: Sequence[str]) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Call handler(args) and return its result; map a raised expected error to its exit code.\n\n    The error's message goes to stderr as one line. Nothing is written to stdout on failure.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        return handler(list(args))\n    except _MAPPED_ERRORS as exc:\n        message = \" \".join(str(exc).split())\n        print(f\"error: {message}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return exc.exit_code\n\n\ndef resolve(name: str) -> Handler:\n    \"\"\"Return the run() of the cli.commands module named by the first argument.\"\"\"\n    if not _COMMAND_NAME.fullmatch(name):\n        raise UsageError(f\"unknown command {name!r}\")\n    module_name = f\"{COMMAND_PACKAGE}.{name}\"\n    try:\n        module = importlib.import_module(module_name)\n    except ModuleNotFoundError as exc:\n        # Only a missing command module is a usage error; a broken import inside one propagates.\n        if exc.name == module_name:\n            raise UsageError(f\"unknown command {name!r}\") from None\n        raise\n    return module.run\n\n\ndef dispatch(argv: Sequence[str]) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Route argv to its command module and return the exit code.\"\"\"\n\n    def route(args: list[str]) -> int:\n        if not args:\n            raise UsageError(\"no command given\")\n        return resolve(args[0])(args[1:])\n\n    return execute(route, argv)\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":8,"oldLines":6,"newStart":8,"newLines":7,"lines":[" from collections.abc import Callable, Sequence"," "," from cli.errors import OperationalError, RejectedFile, UsageError","+from cli.usage import parse"," "," COMMAND_PACKAGE = \"cli.commands\""," _COMMAND_NAME = re.compile(r\"[a-z][a-z0-9_]*\")"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false,"contentNotInModelContext":true},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_014axaQLx2fEHv4jLXi5iXT5","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01TrQo5hph2gkKZon8gNEN8y","type":"tool_result","content":"The file /mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/FxRates/runs/20261027.190646/build/FxRates/cli/dispatch.py has been updated successfully."}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"a9cb209c-cf78-4d6a-b621-670bbb8c6b3d","uuid":"6178fc71-f797-45a2-b8fa-7d8679e2b547","timestamp":"2026-10-27T19:34:32.475Z","tool_use_result":{"filePath":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/FxRates/runs/20261027.190646/build/FxRates/cli/dispatch.py","oldString":"    \"\"\"Route argv to its command module and return the exit code.\"\"\"\n\n    def route(args: list[str]) -> int:\n        if not args:\n            raise UsageError(\"no command given\")\n        return resolve(args[0])(args[1:])\n\n    return execute(route, argv)","newString":"    \"\"\"Validate argv, route it to its command module and return the exit code.\"\"\"\n\n    def route(args: list[str]) -> int:\n        name, command_args = parse(args)\n        return resolve(name)(command_args)\n\n    return execute(route, argv)","originalFile":"\"\"\"Command resolution and the mapping from raised errors to exit codes.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport importlib\nimport re\nimport sys\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Sequence\n\nfrom cli.errors import OperationalError, RejectedFile, UsageError\nfrom cli.usage import parse\n\nCOMMAND_PACKAGE = \"cli.commands\"\n_COMMAND_NAME = re.compile(r\"[a-z][a-z0-9_]*\")\n_MAPPED_ERRORS = (OperationalError, UsageError, RejectedFile)\n\nHandler = Callable[[list[str]], int]\n\n\ndef execute(handler: Handler, args: Sequence[str]) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Call handler(args) and return its result; map a raised expected error to its exit code.\n\n    The error's message goes to stderr as one line. Nothing is written to stdout on failure.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        return handler(list(args))\n    except _MAPPED_ERRORS as exc:\n        message = \" \".join(str(exc).split())\n        print(f\"error: {message}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return exc.exit_code\n\n\ndef resolve(name: str) -> Handler:\n    \"\"\"Return the run() of the cli.commands module named by the first argument.\"\"\"\n    if not _COMMAND_NAME.fullmatch(name):\n        raise UsageError(f\"unknown command {name!r}\")\n    module_name = f\"{COMMAND_PACKAGE}.{name}\"\n    try:\n        module = importlib.import_module(module_name)\n    except ModuleNotFoundError as exc:\n        # Only a missing command module is a usage error; a broken import inside one propagates.\n        if exc.name == module_name:\n            raise UsageError(f\"unknown command {name!r}\") from None\n        raise\n    return module.run\n\n\ndef dispatch(argv: Sequence[str]) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Route argv to its command module and return the exit code.\"\"\"\n\n    def route(args: list[str]) -> int:\n        if not args:\n            raise UsageError(\"no command given\")\n        return resolve(args[0])(args[1:])\n\n    return execute(route, argv)\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":46,"oldLines":11,"newStart":46,"newLines":10,"lines":[" "," "," def dispatch(argv: Sequence[str]) -> int:","-    \"\"\"Route argv to its command module and return the exit code.\"\"\"","+    \"\"\"Validate argv, route it to its command module and return the exit code.\"\"\""," ","     def route(args: list[str]) -> int:","-        if not args:","-            raise UsageError(\"no command given\")","-        return resolve(args[0])(args[1:])","+        name, command_args = parse(args)","+        return resolve(name)(command_args)"," ","     return execute(route, argv)"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false,"contentNotInModelContext":true},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01TrQo5hph2gkKZon8gNEN8y","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011CgTJUuXYGYHJHY3T6WECn","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01Y2dpNNvAvqayADxMYb6Qfc","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/FxRates/runs/20261027.190646/build/FxRates/ecb/history.py","content":"\"\"\"Parse and fully validate an ECB euro reference rate history CSV.\n\nThe parser touches no store. A file that breaks any rule raises RejectedFile before any record is\nreturned, so a caller can never write part of a refused file. Rate text is kept as published;\ndecimal.Decimal is used only to detect a zero value.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport csv\nimport datetime\nimport io\nimport re\nfrom decimal import Decimal\nfrom typing import NamedTuple\n\nfrom cli.errors import RejectedFile\n\nNOT_AVAILABLE = \"N/A\"\n_HEADER_DATE = \"Date\"\n_CURRENCY = re.compile(r\"[A-Z]{3}\")\n_DATE = re.compile(r\"[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}\")\n_RATE = re.compile(r\"[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?\")\n\n\nclass Rate(NamedTuple):\n    \"\"\"One published rate: its date, its currency code and its value as the published text.\"\"\"\n\n    date: str\n    currency: str\n    rate: str\n\n\ndef parse_history(text: str) -> list[Rate]:\n    \"\"\"Return one Rate per non-N/A value in the ECB history text; Rate, parse_history\n\n\ndef _csv(rows: list[list[str]]) -> str:\n    buffer = io.StringIO()\n    writer = csv.writer(buffer, lineterminator=\"\\n\")\n    for row in rows:\n        writer.writerow(row)\n    return buffer.getvalue()\n\n\nHEADER = [\"Date\", \"USD\", \"JPY\", \"HRK\", \"\"]\n\n\ndef test_parse_returns_one_record_per_non_na_value() -> None:\n    text = _csv([\n        HEADER,\n        [\"2025-01-03\", \"1.0299\", \"161.77\", \"N/A\", \"\"],\n        [\"2025-01-02\", \"1.0321\", \"N/A\", \"N/A\", \"\"],\n    ])\n\n    records = parse_history(text)\n\n    assert sorted(records) == sorted([\n        Rate(\"2025-01-03\", \"USD\", \"1.0299\"),\n        Rate(\"2025-01-03\", \"JPY\", \"161.77\"),\n        Rate(\"2025-01-02\", \"USD\", \"1.0321\"),\n    ])\n\n\ndef test_parse_keeps_the_published_text_including_trailing_zeros() -> None:\n    text = _csv([HEADER, [\"2025-01-06\", \"1.10\", \"162.50\", \"N/A\", \"\"]])\n\n    records = parse_history(text)\n\n    assert (\"2025-01-06\", \"USD\", \"1.10\") in records\n    assert (\"2025-01-06\", \"JPY\", \"162.50\") in records\n    assert all(isinstance(record.rate, str) for record in records)\n\n\ndef \"1.0299\")\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\n    \"rows\",\n    [\n        [[\"2025-01-03\", \"1.0299\", \"161.77\", \"\"], [\"2025-01-02\", \"1.0\", \"\"]],\n        [[\"2025-01-03\", \"1.0299\", {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011CgTJVKCqZeweM6oEnbzWY","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01Uioino2K8XkpS8MnBTijFQ","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/FxRates/runs/20261027.190646/build/FxRates/tests/test_ratestore.py","content":"\"\"\"Behavior tests for ratestore.store_rates, run inside the rollback fixture so nothing persists.\"\"\"\n\nfrom persistence.testing import db_session\nfrom ratestore import store_rates\n\nD1 = \"1800-05-01\"\nD2 = \"1800-05-02\"\n\n\ndef test_store_rates_round_trips_exact_text_through_history() -> None:\n    records = [(D1, \"ZZA\", \"1.2300\"), (D1, \"ZZB\", \"10\"), (D2, \"ZZA\", \"1.5\")]\n\n    with db_session() as db:\n        store_rates(db, records)\n\n        zza = db.rates.history(currency=\"ZZA\", start_date=D1, end_date=D2)\n        zzb = db.rates.history(currency=\"ZZB\", start_date=D1, end_date=D2)\n\n        assert [(r.date, r.rate) for r in zza] == [(D1, \"1.2300\"), (D2, \"1.5\")]\n        assert [(r.date, r.rate) for r in zzb] == [(D1, \"10\")]\n\n\ndef test_store_rates_returns_distinct_dates_and_records_written() -> None:\n    records = [(D1, \"ZZA\", \"1.1\"), (D1, \"ZZB\", \"2.2\"), (D2, \"ZZA\", \"3.3\")]\n\n    with db_session() as db:\n        counts = store_rates(db, records)\n\n    assert tuple(counts) == (2, 3)\n\n\ndef test_store_rates_with_empty_input_writes_nothing_and_reports_zero() -> None:\n    with db_session() as db:\n        before = db.rates.list_all()\n\n        counts = store_rates(db, [])\n\n        assert tuple(counts) == (0, 0)\n        assert db.rates.list_all() == before\n\n\ndef test_store_rates_replaces_a_stored_rate_for_the_same_date_and_currency() -> None:\n    with db_session() as db:\n        store_rates(db, [(D1, \"ZZA\", \"1.1\")])\n\n        store_rates(db, [(D1, test_store_rates_replacement_leaves_other_currencies_unchanged() -> None:\n    with db_session() as db:\n        store_rates(db, [(D1, \"ZZA\", \"1.1\"), (D1, \"ZZB\", \"2.2\")])\n\n    store_rates(db, first)\n    again = store_rates(db, first)\n    assert tuple(again) == (1, len(first))\n    rows = db.rates.history(currency=\"ZZA\", start_date=d, end_date=d)\n    assert [(r.date, r.rate) for r in rows] == [(d, first[0][2])]\n    store_rates(db, changed)\n    rows = db.rates.history(currency=\"ZZA\", start_date=d, end_date=d)\n    assert [(r.date, r.rate) for r in rows] == [(d, changed[0][2])]\n    other = db.rates.history(currency=\"ZZB\", start_date=d, end_date=d)\n    assert [(r.date, r.rate) for r in other] == [(d, first[1][2])]\nprint(\"ac ratestore-replace-and-idempotent OK\")\n\nwith db_session() as db:\n    before = len(db.rates.list_all())\n    counts = store_rates(db, [])\n    assert tuple(counts) == (0, 0)\n    assert len(db.rates.list_all()) == before\nprint(\"ac ratestore-empty OK\")\nEOF\nfor f in ac_ecb ac_cli ac_store; do .venv/bin/python -I -c \"import sys; sys.path.insert(0, '.'); exec(open('/tmp/fx-acs/$f.py').read())\" || echo \"FAILED $f\"; done","description":"Check drydock_acceptance import and run declared
